column1: # machorun fixture manifest -- tab separated, one runnable fixture per line.
# id            fixture id; tests/bin/<id> is the Mach-O, tests/expected/<id>.*
# oracle        run                 macOS can execute it, so a baseline exists
#               norun:<reason>      macOS refuses to execute it; no baseline,
# linux         pass                should eventually match the oracle exactly
# Columns are separated by a single TAB. Keep it that way; the harness splits
# on tabs so descriptions may contain spaces.

column5: what

column4: xfail:raw Darwin svc syscalls; on Linux svc traps to the Linux kernel with Linux numbering
column5: no libSystem calls at all - write+exit via svc #0x80

column3: norun:macOS 11+ on arm64 SIGKILLs static executables (no LC_LOAD_DYLINKER)
column4: xfail:no oracle baseline to compare against
column5: fully static, LC_UNIXTHREAD entry, no dyld
LC_MAIN entry, exit status is main's return value
same, classic LC_DYLD_INFO_ONLY fixups
first real libSystem dependency: printf/puts + Darwin varargs
same, classic fixups and __la_symbol_ptr lazy binding
malloc/calloc/realloc/free/strdup/posix_memalign
initialisers via __TEXT,__init_offsets (S_INIT_FUNC_OFFSETS)
same source, initialisers via __DATA_CONST,__mod_init_func
C++ global ctors/dtors, __cxa_atexit, guarded local static
_Thread_local via __thread_vars descriptors and tlv_get_addr
two images: @rpath dylib, data import, reverse import into the exe
same, classic fixups on both images
pthread create/join/mutex/once plus per-thread TLS allocation
Foundation-free Objective-C: classes, selrefs, objc_msgSend
Darwin arm64 varargs in anger: >8 args, interleaved int/double, va_copy, guest va_list into vsnprintf
same source, classic fixups -- the varargs ABI is a libSystem property, not a fixup one
mach_task_self, vm_allocate/protect/deallocate, mach_absolute_time, timebase, mach_error_string
errno numbering, O_* flag values and struct stat layout all differ between Darwin and Linux
a representative hand-built utility: ctype (a DATA table Darwin inlines into the guest), setlocale, getopt, qsort, strftime, fgets
every loaded image sits below 2^47, because libswiftCore has the 47-bit isa mask compiled in
struct dirent is 1048 bytes on Darwin and 280 on glibc, with d_type and d_name at different offsets; readdir translates rather than forwards
condition variables that really block, and the RECURSIVE/ERRORCHECK constants Darwin and glibc swap
all 128 _SC_* names differ between Darwin and glibc, so sysconf must translate rather than forward
struct passwd is 72 bytes on Darwin and 48 on glibc; pw_dir falls off the end of a forwarded one
std::sort really sorts all five hand-instantiated types; the broken version recursed forever
sigset_t is 4 bytes on Darwin and 128 on glibc, ten signal numbers differ, and SIG_BLOCK/UNBLOCK/SETMASK are off by one
Apple's typed allocator; the size argument sits in a different register in every member of the family
walks a real stack through Apple's compact __unwind_info; the symbols resolved the whole time it was stubbed
poll(2) across the boundary: the eight agreeing flags, the counts, and the wrapper's heap path -- a regression guard, since the two flags that differ cannot be reached from a fixture
installing a handler: struct sigaction is 16 bytes against 152, not one sa_flags bit agrees, and the signal NUMBER has to be translated again on the way back INTO guest code
a real C++ throw across frames, caught by type; the case that matters is the handler that must NOT match
fcntl's command agrees and its O_* value does not; madvise's four common advice values agree and MADV_FREE, the only one libdispatch uses, does not
PTHREAD_CREATE_JOINABLE is 1 here and DETACHED there, so the safe-looking direction is the broken one; SCHED_OTHER is glibc's SCHED_FIFO
loading a dylib at RUN TIME: the export trie through a handle, the initialiser, the TLV, and a bind from the new image into an old one
the five MIBs CF needs; KERN_PROC_PID gates __CFInitialize and returns a 648-byte BSD struct CF reads one field from
which image and symbol an address is in, plus RTLD_NEXT/SELF/MAIN_ONLY -- one gap, not three: all of them needed THE CALLING IMAGE
_NSGetExecutablePath must name the GUEST, not the loader -- /proc/self/exe is a real path and the wrong one; plus pthread_atfork, which glibc has no dynamic symbol for
universal binary (x86_64 + arm64); same output as printf, so any diff is a slice-selection bug
